newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul party leader says re-think needed on N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: Seoul party leader says re-think needed on N.Korea.

text.p: South Korea's ruling party chairman on Wednesday said Seoul must re-think its policy towards North Korea, which was grappling with its biggest ever crisis.
Lee Hong-koo of the New Korea Party said the defection by top ideologue Hwang Jang-yop was pushing the North Korean leadership deeper into desperation.
"Severe food shortages and economic difficulties are driving the North Korean system to an irreversible final crisis," Lee told parliament.
"In view of North Korea's rapid breaking away from its orbit and its plunge, we must drastically review our unification policy," he said.
Lee said Seoul's policy of seeking reunification of the Korean peninsula by treating the North as an equal partner might now have to be abandoned.
Seoul's cooperation with its allies on reforming North Korea should also be adjusted.
Lee did not elaborate but a senior New Korea Party official told Reuters the party chairman was bracing South Korea for a possible collapse of the North.
South Korean officials have said problems stemming from the defection of Hwang, a top advisor to North Korean leader Kim Jong-il, were just the start of headaches for Seoul.

Lee said apart from Hwang, who has been marooned at the South Korean consular office in Beijing for eight days, many other North Koreans who had fled the North were awaiting defection to South Korea in China and elsewhere. He did not give details.
South Korean media have reported that Hwang, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy, could be the first in a stream of high-level defectors to betray their Stalinist homeland.
Lee said Hwang must be granted political asylum in South Korea as he wished but urged the South Korean media and citizens to be cautious and patient.
South Korean officials said on Wednesday Seoul's negotiations with Chinese authorities over Hwang's fate had made no progress.
"China has maintained it is desirable that Hwang's case be resolved through South-North Korean dialogue," a Seoul ministry official said, asking not to be identified.
"We are telling the Chinese that there's no dialogue channel and it is impossible to resolve a sensitive defection issue in direct talks with the North," he added.
"But with North Korea changing its attitude, we hope there will be progress in our negotiations," the official said.
Signs have emerged that North Korea might be ready to give up the fight to recover Hwang, possibly as a result of mediation by Beijing to end the Cold War crisis in its backyard.
Japan's economic daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Wednesday that a top North Korean official had said Hwang had already been dismissed by Pyongyang.
Kim Jong-u, head of North Koreas Overseas Economic Cooperation Committee, made the remarks during a meeting with international investment and financial organisations, it said.

The newspaper quoted sources at the meeting as saying that Kim Jong-u was asked if North Korea accepted Hwang's defection. He replied: "That is what the government has decided. The matter is already closed. He has already been dismissed."
"Betraying the people when the country is in great difficulty is an unforgivable act. Because of his old age we will not pursue him," the sources quoted Kim as saying.
